body: Long-running language-model agents depend on persistent memory. Many agent-memory systems preserve history through soft revocation: a contradicted fact is marked invalid and retained rather than deleted. However, whether that mark is enforced at retrieval time is unexamined. In this paper, we measure five such systems: we load each with a revoked policy and its replacement, track whether the revoked fact is returned at retrieval and whether the agent then acts on it across nine policy scenarios and nine models, and score every trial under six defense conditions. We find that no system enforces revocation by default: the revoked fact is returned wherever the revocation label is visible to the retrieval layer, outranks its replacement, and leads agents to the unsafe action. Based on these findings, we develop a guard that sits between the agent and any memory backend and withholds records that are revoked or conflict with their replacement.
summaryZh: 该研究对五种语言模型代理记忆系统进行了实证评估，发现它们在默认情况下未能有效执行事实撤销。当被撤销的事实仍然可见且优先级高于新事实时，代理系统会继续使用旧事实并可能导致不安全行为。研究人员基于此发现，提出了一种新的“守卫”机制，该机制位于代理和记忆后端之间，能够过滤掉被撤销或与新事实冲突的记录，从而增强代理系统的安全性和可靠性。
